rows.ARS:
Medium red Hybrid Tea.
Registration name: DICam
rows.Origin:
Bred by Patrick Dickson (1926-2012) (United Kingdom, before 1965).
Introduced by Unknown (Australia) in 1966 as 'Red Devil'.
Introduced in France by NIRP International / Lux Riviera in 1967 as 'Coeur d'Amour'.
Introduced in United States by Jackson & Perkins Co. (Newark, NY) in 1970 as 'Red Devil'.
rows.Bloom: Scarlet, lighter reverse. Strong fragrance. 72 to 75 petals. Large, very full (41+ petals), high-centered bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season. Ovoid buds.
rows.Habit:
Glossy, dark green foliage.

Height: 3' to 6'7" (90 to 200cm). Width: 2' to 4' (60 to 120cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 4b through 9b. Disease susceptibility: very disease resistant. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that.

rows.Notes:
Arena Rose Co.'s Catalog 2000 says Coeur d'Amour has large, heavily petalled blooms of scarlet-crimson with a lighter reverse... It is more widely known as 'Red Devil'...
The Parentage we list is from Patrick Dickson [see References] for more information.
